newsitem.title: UK: Northern calls for sense in dairy industry.
newsitem.headline: Northern calls for sense in dairy industry.

text.p: Britian's dairy industry has too many players and needs a major merger to sort out the problem of overcapacity, Christopher Haskins, chairman of Northern Foods Plc told reporters on Tuesday.
Britain has some six or seven players, which probably needs to shrink to five in order to make it profitable, said Haskins.
"Based on our strong doorstep delivery business, we are prepared to tough it out until people come to their senses," he said.

Consolidation in the industry is underway worldwide and "we need a big one here," he said. Britain's dairies are under increasing margin pressure from supermarkets, who are pressing for lower prices, while world commodity prices for their by-products like butter fat have fallen sharply.
Dairies have also suffered from a dramatic decline in the amount of milk delivered to the doorstep since the government de-regulated the former Milk Marketing Board in 1994.
Neil Davidson, head of Northern's dairy division, told reporters it chose not to defend its share of milk supply to supermarket chains Iceland Group plc and Somerfield Plc because it was uneconomic.
Profits on the group's milk sales to supermarkets were lower as a result of fierce competition and lower returns from the surplus cream generated by low fat milk production.
But profits on its doorstep delivery business were ahead of last year after a big drive to cut costs and reshape the business.
Britain's dairies include Dairy Crest, Unigate, Robert Wiseman Dairies Plc and MD Foods. Northern Foods is Britain's largest liquid milk company with over 20 percent of the market.
